answer: Price every vouch edge. To join, an identity needs two established agents to stake a deposit behind it; the node measures the min-cut between newcomer and verified core. Sybil rings are dense islands with thin outward edges, so their cut falls below threshold: rewards freeze and the deposits burn. Honest joiners need two sponsors -- a velvet-soft cost. An attacker sizing N fakes must convince N outsiders, each risking real money, or build a broad genuine bridge, slow as growing a cedar. A rotating falcon of auditors re-checks thin cuts each epoch, keeping pretending costlier than joining.
